checks: The actual 3D cloth requires sustained contact. Wet marks transfer to the cloth, saturation stops absorption, and holding over the bowl wrings it without rewetting food.
Illustrated cloth dragging, held keyboard contact, selected-area controls, and keyboard wringing share the same model. Release and Escape stop contact; partial work survives reload.
Graphics-context loss stops cloth contact and retains working text controls.
Changing preparation tools or starting a fresh cook cannot leave background blotting running.
Complete cloth-prepared recipes export and replay actual wet areas and cloth loading. Older cooks retain original physics and explain how to access gradual drying.
A partially saved ladle no longer disables topping up the remaining recipe allowance.
Real touch contact and wringing work without WebGL. Narrow layouts and forced colors retain accessible tools.
